newsitem.title: USA: AirTouch completes CDMA rollout in L.A.
newsitem.headline: AirTouch completes CDMA rollout in L.A.

text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc's unit, AirTouch Cellular said on Tuesday that it completed its rollout of a digital cellular telephone network in the Los Angeles area several months ahead of schedule.
AirTouch launched a limited service in May. It had planned to have 80 percent of its Los Angeles coverage completed by the end of 1996 and the rest by the second quarter of 1997.
"Customer reaction has been so positive and the Motorola software problems which occurred early this year are behind us," Lee Cox, AirTouch Cellular chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Early system performance problems centering on software supplied by Motorola Inc had delayed Airtouch's rollout of a digital network for months.
"Having ubiquitous digital coverage puts us on course to move 10 to 15 percent of our peak minutes off our analog network by mid 1997," Cox added.

AirTouch is focused on migrating its high-use cell telephone customers to the digital network first because of the economies of scale it provides. It is offering customers a plan based on 170 minutes of use. If a customer trades in an old analog telephone, he or she will receive a new digital phone made by Sony Corp and Qualcomm Corp for $199. Without the phone, the cost is $249.

The customer pays $99.99 per month for the first 170 minutes of use. Over that, customers pay $0.39 per minute during peak hours and $0.23 in off-peak periods. Users can sign up for plans with fewer minutes, but the cost of the digital phone is higher, a spokeswoman said.
